title: Packwright app.json
description: What a package folder publishes as: the Win32 app (or Intune Store app) in Intune. Read by Packwright.ps1, Build-IntuneWinApp.ps1, Publish-IntuneWinApp.ps1 and Test-IntuneWinApp.ps1. Everything left out has a default, and a PSADT or MSI package can do without app.json altogether. Keys starting with _ are comments.

$schema.description: This schema, for the editor. Packwright does not read it.

displayName.description: The app's name in Intune and the Company Portal. Left out: PSADT's AppName, the MSI's ProductName, or the .intunewin's file name.

description.description: Shown in the Company Portal. Left out: the display name.

publisher.description: Left out: PSADT's AppVendor or the MSI's Manufacturer, else 'Unknown'.

version.description: The version the app is shown with (Intune's displayVersion). Left out: PSADT's AppVersion or the MSI's ProductVersion.

installCommandLine.description: Run from the extracted package folder, from a 32-bit process. Left out: the standard PSADT command, msiexec /i for an MSI, or powershell.exe/cmd.exe for an Install script. A vendor .exe always needs one.

uninstallCommandLine.description: Left out: as the install command, with msiexec /x <product code> for an MSI and the Uninstall script beside an Install script.

runAsAccount.description: user: the app installs per user, as the person signed in.

maxRunTimeInMinutes.description: How long Intune lets the install run before it calls it failed. Intune's default is 60; Test-IntuneWinApp gives a test install the same time.

returnCodes.description: Added to Intune's own five (0 and 1707 success, 3010 softReboot, 1641 hardReboot, 1618 retry); a code listed here takes the type given. Test-IntuneWinApp judges a test install by the same list.

returnCode.description: An error such as 0x8A150011 is written as the negative number it is in 32 bits: -1978335215.

allowAvailableUninstall.description: Whether the Company Portal offers to uninstall the app when it is assigned as available. Left out: as Intune has it (off for a new app).

isFeatured.description: Whether the Company Portal shows the app among its featured apps. Left out: as Intune has it (off for a new app).

architecture.description: x64 includes ARM64 devices, as Intune has always had it; x64only leaves them out. x86, arm64, a comma list of them, or neutral for all three.

minimumWindowsRelease.description: Intune's own ids: 1607, 1809 and the like, or Windows10_22H2, Windows11_21H2, Windows11_22H2 for newer releases. A bare 22H2 is refused.

icon.description: A png or jpg, beside app.json or by its full path. 256x256 shows sharply in the Company Portal.

detection.description: How Intune tells the app is installed. Left out: the MSI's product code, for an MSI package; anything else needs one.

requirements.description: Script requirement rules: a device that does not meet one reports the app as not applicable, not failed.

dependencies.description: Win32 apps Intune installs first. Set after the upload, without dropping what the app already supersedes.

roleScopeTagIds.description: The ids of the scope tags the app carries, for an account whose Intune role is limited to some (Tenant administration > Roles > Scope tags).

winget.description: Written by Packwright for a package that installs with WinGet; the commands and scripts are written from it. Leave it to Packwright.

wingetRuntime.description: Written by Packwright for the WinGet runtime package. Leave it to Packwright.

intune.description: Written by Publish-IntuneWinApp: the app each tenant has this package as, which the next update goes to. Take it out to publish the folder as a new app.

displayName.description: The name it was published under.

productCode.description: Left out: the product code of the MSI the package holds.

keyPath.description: The app's own key, such as HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\{app}; WOW6432Node is left out and check32BitOn64System set instead.

scriptFile.description: Beside app.json, or a path relative to it. Uploaded as script content, so it need not be in the .intunewin.
